text: 🇲🇽🚆 "The recovery of the trains is a hallmark of the Fourth Transformation." "De la Madrid still made a public investment. With Salinas, no investment at all, and Zedillo privatizes them... and the passenger trains disappear." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 8, 2026 Under Zedillo, freight rail went mainly to Ferromex and Kansas City Southern, now owned by a Canadian company, "with very little regulation." Passenger service shut down except El Chepe. AMLO brought passenger trains back with the Tren Maya and the Interoceanic Train. A constitutional reform to Article 28 now lets the state run passenger trains on existing freight lines.

🚨🇲🇽 "For any collaboration, there is a law, there is a procedure." "In the case of Chihuahua, it was shown that there were people from a US agency in operations on the ground... A case was opened and it is being investigated whether the National Security Law was violated and, if so, what sanctions it would carry and for whom." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 8, 2026 Two people from a US agency died during an operation in Chihuahua; the Attorney General's Office has an open investigation. In Querétaro, the state broke ground on an "International Police Academy" to work with US agencies. Security Secretary García Harfuch reminded Governor Kuri that any collaboration goes through federal law, and Ambassador Johnson replied it will be within Mexican law.
banner: "THERE IS A LAW, THERE IS A PROCEDURE"

text: 🚨🇲🇽 "There is no proof they are linked to any criminal group, nor has any information been received from the United States." "Irregularities, what does that mean? That maybe they haven't properly reported their taxes, their income and expenses... but from there to being linked to a criminal group, well, that's another thing." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 8, 2026 The US Treasury's OFAC sanctioned several companies over alleged Sinaloa Cartel ties, including Inteliproof, which had provided services to Baja California's state prosecutor. Mexico's Financial Intelligence Unit froze accounts over reporting irregularities and gave the companies time to present evidence. It says neither it nor the security cabinet has evidence of cartel links.
banner: OFAC SANCTIONS: NO EVIDENCE, NO US DATA

text: 🇲🇽🚆 "Break-even means they don't require any additional budget support." "...the revenues allow them to operate and maintain their services, and they are all in line with the planning done from the very first moment." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 8, 2026 The state companies run by the Defense Ministry reported: Tren Maya has carried 2.94 million passengers since December 2023, and its revenue grew 96% in 2025 to 541 million pesos. Mexicana now flies 10 Embraer E2s, with passengers up 31% this year. AIFA has broken even since early 2024 and ranks No. 1 in Mexico for air cargo.

🔥🇲🇽 "They live on lies, on gossip." "But it comes out in the Wall Street Journal... They live on lies, on gossip. What should we call them? 'Gossipocrats,' no? Gossips, honestly. There's nothing of substance, nothing of substance." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 8, 2026 Sheinbaum denied a Wall Street Journal report claiming she scolded Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch at a cabinet meeting. She also said Excélsior's front-page "scholarship fraud" story rests on an audit observation that is still unresolved. She cited a new El Heraldo poll putting her approval at 71%.

🇲🇽🇨🇺 "The Cuban doctors are hired directly — that is very important for people to know." "...and with salaries equivalent to what a doctor earns in our country, and they are in places where they are needed, more remote places, where they help us care for the population." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 8, 2026 Asked about staffing Mexico's plan for 12,000 neighborhood clinics, Sheinbaum said the call for 20,000–23,000 health professionals already has 78,000 applicants, mainly Mexican doctors. Washington has imposed visa restrictions on officials linked to Cuba's medical missions, alleging forced labor.
banner: CUBAN DOCTORS: HIRED DIRECT, EQUAL PAY

text: 🇲🇽🔍 "How could one not be happy with these results?" "People in their neighborhood: from half saying they felt unsafe, to 35.9% today. And the trains are doing well, the highways are doing well, the water projects are doing well." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 8, 2026 INEGI's latest survey: the share of adults who feel unsafe in their own neighborhood or locality fell from 50.6% in 2018 to 35.9% in 2026, down 11.4% in the last year alone. Perceived insecurity in their municipality dropped from 70.3% in 2019 to 60.9%.
